title: Asean adopts landmark declaration on space cooperation
summary: MANILA, Philippines — Southeast Asian leaders have adopted the region’s first declaration dedicated exclusively to space cooperation, setting out common priorities for collaboration in space safety…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Southeast Asian leaders have adopted the region’s first declaration dedicated exclusively to space cooperation, setting out common priorities for collaboration in space safety and security, the space economy and workforce development.

The Asean Leaders’ Declaration on the Advancement of Space Science, Technology and Innovation Cooperation was adopted Nov. 15 during the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit in Manila, the Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA) said in a statement Tuesday.

The declaration was spearheaded by the Philippines through PhilSA, the country’s national focal point for space matters under the Asean Subcommittee on Earth, Ocean and Space Science, and the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), which chairs the Asean Committee on Science, Technology and Innovation.

PhilSA said the declaration was among the priority economic deliverables of the Philippines’ Asean chairship. It seeks to establish a common framework for regional cooperation and encourage the joint use of space technologies among member states.

“More than a formal statement, this Declaration reflects a shared regional vision to strengthen collaboration in space science, technology, and innovation. Through this, we hope to further advance Asean’s collective capacity to harness space technologies in support of disaster resilience, environmental sustainability, economic growth, and inclusive development across our region,” PhilSA Director General Gay Jane Perez said.

The declaration identifies three areas for stronger cooperation: space security and safety, the space economy and space workforce development. It also promotes joint research, capacity-building activities and the sharing of space infrastructure and data.
Regional cooperation
According to PhilSA, the agreement builds on several activities organized by the Philippines during its Asean chairship to encourage regional collaboration in space science and technology.

On March 12 and 13, PhilSA, in partnership with the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs and Thailand’s Geo-Informatics and Space Technology Development Agency, held a seminar-workshop in Manila on space situational awareness and space traffic management.
The event brought together Asean representatives, policymakers, technical experts and commercial operators to discuss regional approaches to space safety, data sharing and operational coordination.

PhilSA also organized the Asean Space Forum: Navigating Our Future through Space Diplomacy during Philippine Space Week 2026 to discuss the proposed declaration, build partnerships and explore opportunities for regional cooperation in the global space sector.
Space economy
The potential of space technology for business and economic development was also discussed during the Asean Business and Investment Summit 2026 in Pasay City on Nov. 15.

In a keynote address, Japanese astronaut and Axiom Space chief technology officer for Asia Pacific Dr. Koichi Wakata discussed opportunities for the Philippines and other Asean countries in space research, advanced manufacturing and human spaceflight as commercial access to orbit expands.
A panel discussion titled “Space Economy: Asean’s Next Frontier” also explored how space technology could create business opportunities and contribute to everyday life across Southeast Asia.

Moderated by PhilSA founding Director General and University of the Philippines Vice President for Research and Innovation Dr. Joel Joseph Marciano Jr., the panel included Wakata, Hidetaka Aoki of Space Port Japan, Christian Patouraux of Kacific, Robbie Schingler of Planet and Ramon Garcia Jr. of Ascend International Gateway.

The discussion covered opportunities across the space industry, including satellite manufacturing, ground infrastructure, data analytics, connectivity and commercial applications. It also examined how Asean could develop a competitive and sustainable regional space economy.
To further explore opportunities for the Philippine space sector, PhilSA will hold Space Partnerships, Acceleration, Research, Commercialization and Synergies (SPARCS) 2026 on Nov. 23.

The event will gather representatives from government, industry, academe, startups, investment and research institutions, and development partners. Discussions will cover ways to strengthen the country’s capabilities in space manufacturing, spaceport and commercial launch services, and the development of applications and services using space technology.
Next steps
PhilSA is also set to hold a virtual ceremonial launch of the Asean Declaration on Space Cooperation and a forum on Dec. 7 under the theme “Navigating Asean’s Future in Space, Together.”

The event will bring together representatives from Asean member states, dialogue partners and other stakeholders to discuss the declaration’s provisions and identify opportunities to translate its commitments into regional initiatives.

“The adoption reaffirms Asean’s shared commitment to harnessing space science, technology, and innovation for sustainable development, regional resilience, and a more connected and collaborative space community,” PhilSA said in a statement. /dm
